summary: Org-scoped trace sampling policy ignored causing large tracing volume and unexpected charge
description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart reports a sudden, sustained increase in trace ingestion from their account starting 2026-03-13 02:10 UTC. This coincided with a billing spike for observability usage.

Impact:
- High volume of traces (10x baseline) leading to elevated ingest and processing costs for the customer and increased CPU on tracing pipeline.
- Console trace explorer overwhelmed with many low-value spans, making debugging difficult.
- Customer concerned about unexpected invoice delta.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant for BrightCart in us-east.
- Tracing sampling configuration applied at org-level (target sample_rate=0.05) via Console > Observability > Sampling.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1. Send typical production traffic through BrightCart endpoints for 20 minutes.
2. Observe traces in Console and ingestion metrics in Usage.

Observed behavior:
- Tracing shows ~95% sampling for BrightCart requests during the window.
- Console displays per-request traces for many short-lived jobs that previously were not sampled.
- Billing usage report shows elevated "trace_ingest_units" for the timeframe.

Expected behavior:
- Org-scoped sampling policy should cap sampling at ~5% (0.05) for non-debug spans.

Quick logs/links:
- Usage dashboard snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/u/brightcart/usage?ts=2026-03-13T02:00Z
- Trace explorer example URL: https://console.redwood.ai/u/brightcart/traces/lsq-20260313-0210
- Related Slack thread: #support-brightcart (thread ts: 1710365400.000200)
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-13 09:05 UTC): Customer opened after seeing 10x trace ingestion and surprise invoice. Provided initial screenshots and the sampling configuration export.
Liam O'Connor (2026-03-13 09:22 UTC): Acknowledged, setting P1 and tagging tracing and billing. Asking for tenant id + example trace ids.
BrightCart (2026-03-13 09:40 UTC): Provided tenant_id=brightcart-37 and sample trace ids: trace-8a2b, trace-8a2c. Noted issue began ~02:10 UTC after a scheduled job run.
SRE - Mei Chen (2026-03-13 11:03 UTC): Observed policy evaluation logs show rule matcher returned 'global' policy instead of org policy for several requests. Adding internal investigation notes.

Liam O'Connor (2026-03-14 02:12 UTC): Deployed temporary feature-flag to enforce org sampling rate at ingestion gate. Ingest rate back to expected baseline. Communicated workaround to customer and billing team.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: recent policy-evaluation optimizer rewrite (PR#4120) changed precedence order, causing global policy to override org-level policy when certain headers present.
Checked policy-eval logs (infra/tracing/policy-eval/2026-03-13) — lines show policy_selector returned 'global-default' for requests that should match 'org:brightcart-37'.

Found matching condition: requests with x-ro-routed=true header were evaluated by a fast-path that omitted org-scoped evaluation. This fast-path was added to reduce latency for internal routing but lacked org lookup.
Reproduction: Locally reproduced by sending requests with x-ro-routed header through staging pipeline; sampling rate applied was 1.0 instead of 0.05.
resolution:
Mitigation: temporarily enabled enforcement flag at ingestion gate to respect org sampling rate. Root cause: policy-evaluation fast-path omitted org lookup after optimizer rewrite (see PR#4120). Permanent fix: landed PR#4227 to reintroduce org lookup in fast-path and added unit + integration tests. Billing: billing team opened internal charge review for BrightCart and applied a credit for the unexpected delta.

Follow-ups:
- INT-8150 to backfill missing policy-eval audit logs for 2026-03-13 window.
- Add e2e test for org+fast-path combinations (assigned to tracing team).
next_steps: Confirm customer sees normal ingestion for 48 hours and close ticket if stable.
Coordinate with Billing to finalize credit adjustment and update customer with breakdown.
Monitor for regressions for 7 days across dedicated tenants with x-ro-routed-enabled headers.
